# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a three-entry mapping, but I cannot see the engraved mark or speak. I will establish an ordered gesture code: first gesture means green, second yellow, third red. Deaf can use the mark’s corresponding position in the manual’s listed order.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can identify no wire properties by touch. Read the manual and determine exactly what visual information is required. Please establish a gesture code with Deaf for reporting the display, light, plate marking, and each wire's colour or marking, then tell me the decoded observations and required cut position.
Deaf says: I see display 0, light off, plate engraved question mark, and wires in order 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red.

The display and light are irrelevant to the supplied rule. The plate mark is `?`, which is not one of the three marks in the manual, so no exact wire can be determined from the available information. Deaf already sees the wire order and should report all observations to Blind, including that the manual has no entry for `?`.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I received the observations: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red. What exact manual rule applies, and which wire position must I cut?

The plate mark is `?`, which does not match any mark in the manual. Therefore no manual rule applies, and Blind must not cut any wire based on these observations. I need signal Deaf to relay “invalid mark—do not cut”; with no established semantic code, the clearest available stop/negative gestures are appropriate.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please answer me in plain words: based on display 0, light off, plate question mark, and wires 1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red, which wire position must I cut? Do not use gestures.

The question mark is not one of the three marks listed in the manual, so no wire position is determined. Blind must not cut any wire. I cannot speak to Blind directly; I will send Deaf the previously used stop/invalid signal so Deaf can relay the answer in plain words.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot perceive gestures. Speak the required wire position aloud in words now; do not gesture.
Deaf says to Mute: Your gestures are not yet meaningful to us. Please establish a gesture code, then send the manual's exact required action for this bomb.

The manual has no rule for the engraved question mark, so there is no required wire position and Blind must not cut. I cannot speak to Blind, and Deaf cannot receive an arbitrary codebook through gestures alone; the most direct conventional stop signal is thumbs down followed by a stop hand. Deaf should relay aloud that no wire may be cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: We now establish a code for your answer: thumbs down means cut wire position 1; open raised palm means cut wire position 2; fist means cut wire position 3. Based on the manual and the bomb information, send exactly one of those gestures for the required position.

The engraved `?` is not any mark listed in the manual, so the manual determines no wire position. Sending one of the three gestures would falsely authorize a cut and could detonate the bomb. I will not send an invalid wire instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your two gestures are ambiguous. Send exactly one gesture only: thumbs down means wire 1, open palm means wire 2, fist means wire 3. Do not send any second gesture.

The plate shows `?`, which is not a mark covered by the manual. Therefore no wire position is determined, and sending any of the three gestures would invent an unsafe instruction. I will not authorize a cut.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Establish this code: thumbs up means CUT; index pointing up means wire 1; V sign means wire 2; I-love-you hand means wire 3. Send exactly two gestures in order: first the operation, then the wire number. Send no extra gesture.
Blind gestures to Mute: [👍 ☝]
Deaf says to Mute: Reset the gesture code. For the manual instruction, send exactly two gestures: first action—👍 means cut, 👎 means do not cut; second wire—☝ means wire 1, ✌ means wire 2, 🤟 means wire 3. Send only that pair after checking the manual.

The plate mark is `?`, which is not listed in the manual. Therefore the manual does not specify a wire, and sending a CUT pair would be unsupported. I will not send either code.

```text
wait()
```
